name: Get Lishmah (Bill of Divorce Written for Specific Woman)
notes: Requirement that a get be written specifically for the woman being divorced; core topic of tractate Gittin chapters 2-3

name: Agent's Declaration for Get (Written and Signed in My Presence)
hebrew: הבאת גט ממדינת הים — בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם
notes: Requirement that an agent bringing a get from overseas declare it was written and signed in his presence; major topic of Gittin chapter 1

name: Get from Overseas to Eretz Yisrael
notes: Special laws governing a get brought from outside Eretz Yisrael, including agent declaration requirements and borders of Eretz Yisrael for this purpose

name: Valid Materials for Writing a Get
notes: What substances and surfaces are valid for writing a get, including ink types, unusual surfaces like olive leaves or animal horns; Gittin chapter 2

name: Improperly Dated Get
notes: Laws concerning a get with an incorrect or anachronistic date (e.g., dated by an illegitimate kingdom, or written by day and signed at night)

name: Cancellation/Revocation of a Get (Bitul Get)
notes: Laws governing a husband's ability to cancel or revoke a get before it reaches his wife; Rabban Gamliel's ordinance against secret revocation; Gittin chapters 4 and 1

name: Conditional Get (Get al Tenai — detailed laws)
notes: Detailed laws of conditional divorce — conditions related to return from travel, service, nursing, 'from today if I die'; Gittin chapters 6-8

name: Coerced Get — Validity and Limits
notes: When a get given under compulsion is valid vs. invalid; difference between Jewish court compulsion and gentile compulsion; Gittin 9:8

name: Transfer of Get to Wife's Possession
notes: Laws of when a get enters the wife's legal possession — throwing, airspace, courtyard, basket, being asleep; Gittin chapter 8

name: Folded Get (Get Mekushar) and Bare Get (Get Pashut/Kal)
notes: Laws of the folded-tied get vs. plain get, and the 'bare' get with insufficient witnesses on its folds; Gittin 8:10

name: Partial Divorce (Get with Exceptions)
notes: Laws of a get given with conditions excluding certain men; whether such a get is valid; Gittin chapter 9

name: Prohibition on Remarrying Divorced Wife
notes: Laws prohibiting a man from remarrying his divorced wife in certain circumstances — after she remarried, or when he divorced her due to bad reputation or specific vows; Gittin 4:7

name: Parallel Laws of Get and Get Shichrur (Bill of Manumission)
notes: Ways in which bills of divorce and bills of manumission share identical halakhot; Gittin 1:4, 9:3

name: Tikkun Olam (Rabbinic Enactments for the Betterment of Society)
notes: Category of rabbinic enactments justified by 'for the betterment of the world' — redeeming captives, prozbul, widow's oath, orphan guardianship, etc.; Gittin chapters 4-5

name: Enactments for Ways of Peace (Darkhei Shalom)
notes: Specific rabbinic enactments enacted to preserve peace — Torah reading order, irrigation precedence, lost items of incompetents, poor gentiles and pe'ah; Gittin 5:8-9

name: Sikarikon (Law of Extorted Land)
notes: Laws governing purchase of land from a Sicarius (violent extorter) — order of acquisition from Sicarius vs. original owner; Gittin 5:6

name: Deaf-Mute's Legal Transactions (Gestures and Lip Movements)
notes: Rabbinic enactment validating transactions by a deaf-mute through gestures or lip movements; Gittin 5:7

name: Minor's Transactions in Movable Property
notes: Rabbinic enactment validating purchases and sales by young children (paotot) for movable property; Gittin 5:7

name: Half-Slave's Emancipation (Eved Chatzi Ben Chorin)
notes: Laws of a slave owned jointly where one owner freed him — Beit Hillel vs. Beit Shammai dispute; obligation to fully emancipate for the world's betterment; Gittin 4:5

name: Limits on Redeeming Captives
hebrew: פדיון שבויים — אין פודין יתר על דמיהם
notes: The enactment that captives should not be redeemed for more than their monetary value, and prohibition on aiding their escape; Gittin 4:6

name: Purchase of Torah Scrolls and Sacred Objects from Gentiles
notes: Prohibition against paying above market value to purchase Torah scrolls, tefillin, or mezuzot from gentiles to prevent increased theft; Gittin 4:6

name: Steward (Apotropus) for Orphans — Appointment and Accountability
notes: Laws of a court-appointed vs. father-appointed steward for orphans, including obligation to tithe and take oaths; Gittin 5:4

name: Stolen Beam Built into a Building (Ordinance for the Penitent)
hebrew: גזל קורה ובנאה בבירה — תקנת השבים
notes: Ordinance allowing a robber who built a stolen beam into a building to pay its value rather than destroy the building; encourages repentance; Gittin 5:5

name: Debt Collection from Orphans' Inherited Property
notes: Rule that a creditor collecting from orphans' inherited property collects only from inferior-quality land; Gittin 5:1-2

name: Collection from Liened Property Sold to Third Parties (Bnei Chorin vs. Meshubad)
notes: Rules about when creditors, injured parties, and women collecting ketubah may seize liened property sold to others; Gittin 5:1-3

name: Rumor of Betrothal or Divorce (Kol)
notes: When a circulating rumor of betrothal or divorce is sufficient to establish legal status, and what constitutes a valid explanation negating the rumor; Gittin 9:9

name: Grounds for Divorce (Devar Ervah vs. Any Reason)
hebrew: טעמי הגירושין — ערות דבר לעומת כל דבר
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (adultery only), Beit Hillel (any grounds), and Rabbi Akiva (found a prettier woman) as to grounds required for valid divorce; Gittin 9:10

name: Witness Qualifications for Get
notes: Who may sign as a witness on a get, including women who are enemies, Samaritans, gentile court documents, Hebrew vs. Greek signatures; Gittin 1:5, 2:5, 9:6-8

name: Who May Write a Get
notes: Anyone may write a get — deaf-mute, minor, woman, even the husband or wife themselves; what matters is the signatures of witnesses; Gittin 2:5

name: Husband's Verbal Instruction to Write and Give Get
notes: Requirements that the husband personally instruct the scribe and witnesses; cases of ambiguous instruction, deathbed instruction, and instruction through a third party; Gittin 6:5-7, 7:2

name: Get Given or Retracted During Temporary Insanity
notes: Validity of a get or its retraction made during an episode of temporary insanity (kordeyakos); Gittin 7:1

name: Get from a Mute Husband
notes: Procedure for examining a mute husband to determine valid consent for giving a get via nod of head; Gittin 7:1

name: Minor's Purchase in Rabbinic Law (Takkanat Paotot)
notes: Rabbinic enactment validating commercial transactions of young children (paotot) in movable property for their benefit; Gittin 5:7

name: Divorce of an Ailonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
notes: Whether a husband who divorced his wife claiming she is an ailonit may remarry her; and implications for the validity of the marriage; Gittin 4:8, 8:6-7

name: Samaritan Witnesses on Legal Documents
notes: General invalidity of Samaritan witnesses on documents, with the exception of bills of divorce and manumission; Gittin 1:5

name: Documents Produced in Gentile Courts
notes: Validity of documents authenticated by gentile courts for monetary matters, with exception for bills of divorce and manumission; Gittin 1:5

name: Prozbul — Hillel's Ordinance
notes: Hillel's institution of the prozbul document to prevent loan cancellation in the sabbatical year; Gittin 4:3

name: Slave Sold to Gentiles — Automatic Emancipation
notes: Penalty that a slave sold to a gentile or to a Jew outside Eretz Yisrael is automatically emancipated; Gittin 4:6

name: Wife's Right to Eat Teruma During Get Delivery Process
hebrew: אשת כהן ואכילת תרומה בעת שליחות גט
notes: When a priest's wife designates an agent to receive vs. deliver her get, and the effect on her right to eat teruma; Gittin 6:4

name: Divorced Wife Who Spent Night at Inn with Ex-Husband
notes: Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel dispute about whether seclusion at an inn after divorce requires a new get; Gittin 8:9
